facts.text: Burlington began as Foxville in 1835, founded by Moses Smith and William Whiting, and was renamed Burlington in 1839 after the Vermont city.
The first railroad to reach Burlington ran in 1855, built by the Racine, Janesville and Mississippi Railroad before joining the Chicago, Milwaukee and St. Paul line.
Since 1928 the Burlington Historical Society has kept the town’s heritage alive, offering a museum and a log cabin for visitors to explore.
Burlington Academy opened in 1844 as the town’s first private school, created after residents grew dissatisfied with existing schools.
In 1966 the Ardagh plant was built to serve Miller Brewing Company, marking a significant industrial development in the town.
